title: Delta Queen cruise, gambling and Sharky-era earnings
summary: The 1971 Delta Queen trip with Ellen, a gambling death in Arkansas, and earnings with Sharky.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did she go with you when you went to Chicago and played at the Palmer House?

No. No. But she did make a trip with me 22 days on the Delta Queen when I played on the Delta Queen. Mm-hmm. All the way from New Orleans to Cincinnati to St. Paul. I wouldn't go without her. Got a fabulous salary of $175 a week, a stateroom, board for me and her, and plane flight back from St. Paul to New Orleans. 22 days long. When was that?
Well, you couldn't spend any money on the boat, huh, Much? No. Did you gamble? Oh, no. I never gambled. I would think that'd be one thing to do on the boats, river boats. That's traditional.

When I was playing with Tony Foucherat and Mutt Powers and Flavor Ford, like I told you, we were playing in Smack Over Arkansas at one time. No. Tony wasn't in that band. I was with Happy Cook and Little Chink Martin, Charlie DuPont, Harry Shields. When we were playing at a gambling place about five miles out of Smack Over Arkansas, when gambling was strictly against the law, on New Year's Eve night, I saw a man walk out after losing everything in the world he had. I couldn't get to him in time. He blew his brains out right in my presence. I never gambled since. I never have played the horses, but once in my life, and I lost two dollars, and that broke me. That cured me of the thought. Poor Santo, when we were playing with Sharky, you know, we made up to five hundred dollars a week with Sharky. And five hundred a week in those days, in 1946 and seven and eight and nine, fifty, five hundred dollars was two thousand dollars today. And you know that's true. stuff
